Install it using the plugin marketplace:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add tester-army/e2e
claude plugin install e2e@e2e
```

Then start a new session after installing.

When no reference screenshot exists, the first test run creates one but fails, so developers should inspect and commit the image before rerunning. Screenshot files should be committed alongside the corresponding tests. Each target and operating system uses separate snapshot files because fonts and rendering differ.

The authentication token should be read from `request.env` provided to `DeviceProvider.acquire`, rather than directly from `process.env`.

For local development, developers can authenticate using an existing subscription, such as ChatGPT Plus or Pro, by running `npx e2e login openai`, or configure an AI SDK provider with the required API credentials. In CI environments, authentication should use API keys provided through environment variables. These credentials should be stored as CI secrets. API keys should only be made available to trusted builds to prevent unauthorized access.

For an iOS Expo development build, developers can configure `app.launchArguments` with `--initialUrl` pointing to the development server. Camera access can be granted through `app.permissions` by setting `camera: 'grant'`, which prevents a system permission prompt. Each test should begin with `app.open()` because the initial warm-up does not apply the configured launch arguments or permissions.

Developers can start an authenticated exploration using `npx e2e explore --session admin 'Explore the admin settings'`, provided a setup test saves the named session. The explorer runs only the corresponding setup test and restores its session before starting. To keep screenshots available, the setup can authenticate through a session cookie using `browser.setCookies` instead of filling a secret, since a password fill disables screenshots for the restored exploration.

The decision-model executor selects the `type` operation and identifies a target field from the latest screen observation. A separate text model then generates the input value using the goal, parameters, field label, and page text. The executor enters exactly the generated string into the selected field.

The Ubuntu image provides three preconfigured Android AVDs: `emulator` (API 34), `emulator-35`, and `emulator-36`.

Limrun provides five device configuration options: `region`, `hardTimeout`, `ios.model`, `android.model`, and `android.osVersion`. By default, Limrun selects the region, but a preferred region such as `eu` may overflow to another region when capacity is limited. The `hardTimeout` option limits the maximum device lifetime, including abandoned runs, defaults to `1h`, and accepts Go-style durations. Limrun selects device models by default, with `iphone` or `ipad` for iOS and `phone` or `tablet` for Android, while `android.osVersion` defaults to `15` and serves as a scheduling hint.

A pre-page script lets developers prepare browser behavior before the application starts, such as mocking a browser API, seeding `Math.random`, or setting a flag the app reads at boot.
The failure recap displays the recording's file path, or its URL if a hosted browser retains the video remotely.

Use ordinary Node.js code directly in the test instead of dedicated e2e equivalents. For example, use `fetch` for HTTP requests, `fs` for filesystem operations, or an application's database client for database access.

e2e does not yet support Playwright's `locator.and(other)`, `locator.or(other)`, or `locator.locator('css')` methods. For nested selectors, developers can use scoped semantic queries such as `cell.getByRole('textbox')`, chain `getByRole(...)` after `browser.locator('css')`, or express the entire path in a single `browser.locator` selector. The migration table lists no direct equivalents for `locator.and` or `locator.or`.
The JSON-only restriction allows e2e to record and redact the result in the test report.

Maestro's `tapOn: "Save"` becomes `screen.getByText('Save').tap()`, while a conditional `runFlow` becomes `if (await locator.isVisible()) { ... }`. Maestro uses case-insensitive regular-expression matching and taps the first match, whereas e2e matches strings exactly and case-sensitively and raises `LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS` on multiple matches. Use `{ exact: false }` or a regular expression for flexible text matching, and `.first()` or `{ visible: true }` to narrow multiple matches.

For autocomplete fields that react to keyboard events, use `pressSequentially()` instead of `fill()`, which sets the value without emitting keyboard events. The `pressSequentially()` method uses the platform keyboard and supports a delay between characters. When no text-accepting field has focus, a custom engine's `EngineKeyboard.type` must throw `NOT_ACTIONABLE` rather than silently discard the input.
It throws `INVALID_LOCATOR` for a negative or non-integer index.

Built-in resources are lazy and acquired only when requested, whereas every custom definition in an `extend()` chain runs for each registered case, even if it is never named. Custom setup can therefore open pages or change application state despite appearing unused.
Each engine maps its platform's element types onto e2e's shared, closed `Role` vocabulary, allowing the same role query to work across browser and device targets.
An `agent.act` instruction must contain between 1 and 8192 UTF-8 bytes after NFC normalization.

The `toBeVisible()` assertion repeatedly checks for one visible match until the condition holds or its timeout expires. If no element appears, the assertion eventually fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED`; a hidden element also keeps it waiting for visibility. By contrast, `locator.isVisible()` reads the current state immediately and returns `false` for an absent or hidden element.

Without `--update-snapshots`, an assertion against a baseline written earlier in the same run fails with `ASSERTION_FAILED` until the next run. A negated assertion cannot pass against such a baseline, even with the flag. With `--update-snapshots`, a positive assertion can compare against the baseline and may rewrite it.

A client disconnect or termination signal returns `0`, an uncaught error returns `1`, and invalid command-line arguments return `2`. Startup failures use the underlying error's category-specific status instead.

Press `f` to rerun previously unsuccessful tests, even outside the current positional and `p` selection. Press `u` to rerun the current selection with `--update-snapshots`. Press `p` to select a file, bare name, or glob for subsequent runs. Press `t` to filter by test-title pattern.
The security policy forbids serializing secret values into JSON. When a `Secret` handle reaches such a sink, e2e rejects the operation with `POLICY_DENIED`.

The variables `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` and `GITHUB_REF` identify the pull request, with the event payload also supplying its head commit. The variables `GITHUB_WORKFLOW` and `GITHUB_JOB` form the marker used to find the reporter's existing comment on reruns. The variables `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and `GITHUB_RUN_ID` build the artifact link.

Under `on-all-retries`, e2e retains a trace page for each test that was retried. By contrast, video captures every attempt after the first, rather than the initial attempt. If no retry occurs, neither a trace page nor a video is produced under this mode.

Set `maxObservationBytes` and `maxInputTokens` on the named agents under `agents`. Each worker constructs its own agents from the configuration module. The report records the largest per-agent observation budget in `run.limits.maxObservationBytes` and the largest input-token budget in `run.limits.maxModelTokensPerCall`.
The `doGenerate` method provides the generation call that distinguishes a live AI SDK model instance from its three identifying strings alone.
Developers must manually add the custom results directory to `.gitignore`, because `e2e init` creates ignore entries only for the default `.e2e/` paths.
Each worker constructs its own custom `store` instance, so workers cannot rely on sharing one constructed instance.
The `app` fields explicitly accept `undefined` in their types, allowing environment variables to be used directly even when unset.

The runner uses `WORKER_EXIT` for an unexpected worker termination during file execution, whereas `WORKER_CRASH` identifies the test active when the worker exited. Remaining tests in that file are skipped. Attempts completed before the exit remain in the report, including earlier retries and finished serial-group members.
